purpose: Divalproex is used to treat seizures, bipolar disorder (to help control mood swings), and to prevent migraine headaches. Your doctor may prescribe it for one or more of these conditions. It helps keep your brain activity more stable and balanced.
how_it_works: Your brain uses chemical signals to communicate, and sometimes those signals can get out of balance or fire too fast. Divalproex works by increasing a calming chemical in your brain called GABA, which helps slow down and steady those signals. Think of it like a dimmer switch that helps prevent your brain from getting overloaded.
common_side_effects: Nausea, upset stomach, or vomiting (especially when starting); drowsiness or feeling tired; dizziness; weight gain; hair thinning or hair loss; shaky hands (tremor); and diarrhea. Taking it with food can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: This medication can rarely cause serious liver damage or a dangerous condition called pancreatitis — contact your doctor right away if you have stomach pain, yellowing of your skin or eyes, or unusual fatigue. It must NOT be used during pregnancy as it can cause serious birth defects. Regular blood tests are needed to monitor your liver and medication levels. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor.
typical_dosing: Dosing is very individualized and depends on what condition is being treated. For seizures or bipolar disorder, doses typically start low and are slowly increased, often ranging from 250 mg to 1500 mg or more per day, divided into doses or taken once daily with the extended-release form. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on how you respond and your blood levels. Always take it exactly as prescribed.
